notes.5: This question was not well answered. All the other options were more popular than the correct answer. Option A was the most common incorrect answer, suggesting poor recall of ionic bonding.
notes.6: The distribution of answers suggests that many candidates were guessing. When answering questions like this, candidates are advised to consider a simple compound they know well and to check whether the statements they choose can be applied to that compound.
notes.10: Calculations are often found to be demanding. Although the correct answer was the most chosen option overall, option A was a common incorrect answer.
notes.11: Some candidates were more likely to choose any one of the other answers rather than the correct answer. Option A was the most popular choice overall. The difference between reaction products when electrolysing molten rather than aqueous electrolytes was often not well recalled.
notes.13: Fewer than one in five candidates answered this correctly. Option C was the most common incorrect answer with candidates confusing endothermic and exothermic reactions.
notes.14: Most candidates correctly identified that decreasing the concentration would not lead to an increase in reaction rate. The impact of changes to the surface area of a solid was not so well recalled and option C was chosen almost as commonly as the correct answer.
notes.20: Candidates appear to have recalled that lead compounds are frequently insoluble, but did not always recall that all nitrates are soluble. Option B was the most chosen answer. A significant number of candidates chose option D, perhaps confusing sodium carbonate with calcium carbonate.
notes.21: Most candidates recognised that the element could not be from Group VIII of the Periodic Table. Fewer candidates recalled that transition elements typically have high melting points and form coloured compounds. Over a third of the candidates chose option D.
notes.27: The link between reactivity and the extraction of the metal from its oxide using carbon is a common cause for confusion. Option C was chosen by a third of the candidates.
notes.34: Few candidates mistook the structure in option A for ethanoic acid. The structure shown for the correct answer, option C, appeared to confuse candidates and so options B and D were more likely to be chosen. Candidates are reminded that carbon will only form four covalent bonds.
notes.35: Option A was the most popular answer. Candidates are reminded that petroleum is a mixture of different hydrocarbons which must be separated before any use is to be made of them. Fractional distillation must therefore be the first stage.
notes.39: Nearly all candidates identified option D as being incorrect. Other solid mixtures given in options A and B, were not so readily rejected.
notes.general_comments:
Candidates found Questions 4, 8, 24, 26 and 30 to be least demanding and Questions 5, 6, 11, 13, 20, 27
and 34 to be most demanding.
Syllabus content about types of bonding and the properties of substances was often not well recalled.
